title: Removal of the Rear Pressure Bulkhead Outboard Bracket and Segment Root Shear Tie
abstract: Removal of the outboard bracket and the segment root shear tie from the rear pressure bulkhead, required before any repair of the web or replacement of the radial stiffener attachment.

sections.purpose: This task removes the outboard bracket and the segment root shear tie from one radial segment of the rear pressure bulkhead, so that the web can be repaired or the attachment renewed.
sections.job_setup_note: The bulkhead is a pressure boundary. Every fastener removed must be accounted for and recorded on the removal sheet, and no fastener hole may be left open when the aircraft is unattended. Work from a platform inside the tail cone; do not stand on the bulkhead web at any time. The cabin must be depressurised and the outflow valve locked open.
sections.procedure: 1. Confirm that the cabin is depressurised and that the outflow valve is locked open. 2. Get access through the aft cargo compartment in zones 143 and 146 and through the tail cone in zone 193. 3. Install the working platform inside the tail cone. WARNING: DO NOT STAND ON THE PRESSURE BULKHEAD WEB. USE THE PLATFORM ONLY. 4. Remove the sealant fillet from around the bracket D5331131182950 with a plastic scraper. 5. Record the position of every fastener on the removal sheet. 6. Remove the fasteners from the bracket and lift it clear. CAUTION: SUPPORT THE BRACKET BEFORE YOU REMOVE THE LAST FASTENER. IT WEIGHS MORE THAN 25 KILOGRAMS AND WILL FALL. 7. Remove the clevis pins AGS566056-63 that retain the segment root shear tie D5331135070611. 8. Remove the shear tie and put it on a padded surface. 9. Do a detailed visual inspection of the exposed web and record every finding. 10. Where the lug GIR251836-67 is to be renewed, remove it now and keep the shim pack with its position marked. 11. Protect the open fastener holes with temporary plugs if the aircraft is to be left.
sections.close_out: Bag and label the removed fasteners. Confirm that the removal sheet shows every fastener accounted for. Cover the exposed web area to keep it clean. Make an entry in the aircraft technical log that the pressure boundary is open and that the aircraft must not be pressurised.

safety_precautions: Make sure that the cabin is depressurised and the outflow valve is locked open.
Do not stand on the pressure bulkhead web.
Account for every fastener removed on the removal sheet.
Support heavy parts before you remove the last fastener.
